name: web_stream_close
signature: int web_stream_close("ID=<n>", LAST);
description: Closes a media stream previously opened with web_stream_open and releases the streaming connection resources. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success or LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: web_stream_get_param_double
signature: double web_stream_get_param_double(const char *StreamID, const int StateType);
description: Retrieves status information from an open stream as a double value (for example, the current time position or the duration). Returns a negative integer on failure.

args.name: StreamID
args.desc: The identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: StateType
args.desc: The status type: CURRENT_TIME (2), CURRENT_BUFFERING_TIME (3), TOTAL_BUFFERING_TIME (4), BUFFERED_TIME (5), or DURATION (6).

name: web_stream_get_param_int
signature: int web_stream_get_param_int(const char *StreamID, const int StateType);
description: Returns the status of an open stream as an integer, either the current state or the number of bytes received. Returns -1 on failure.

args.name: StreamID
args.desc: The identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: StateType
args.desc: CURRENT_STATE (one of the states STREAM_STATUS_INIT, _PLAY, _PAUSE, _STOP, and so on) or BYTES_RECEIVED (the number of bytes received).

name: web_stream_get_param_string
signature: int web_stream_get_param_string(const char *StreamID, const int StateType, const char *ParameterName);
description: Retrieves a string-valued status from an open stream and saves it to a script parameter. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success or LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: StreamID
args.desc: The identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: StateType
args.desc: STREAM_URL (7), PROTOCOL (8), or SERVER_IP (9).

args.name: ParameterName
args.desc: The name of the parameter in which the resulting string is saved.

name: web_stream_open
signature: int web_stream_open("ID=<string>", "URL=<url>", "Protocol=<protocol>", ["Bandwidth=<n>"], ["StreamBufferingTimeout=<seconds>"], ["DumpPath=<path>"], ["EventReportCB=<function_name>"], ["AdaptiveMode=<0 or 1>"], ["Duration=<seconds>"], LAST);
description: Opens (starts) a media stream and creates a stream identifier for use by subsequent web_stream_* functions. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success or LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: ID
args.desc: A unique stream identifier (integer > 0) referenced by other stream functions.

args.name: URL
args.desc: The full address of the media resource.

args.name: Protocol
args.desc: The communication protocol: HTTP or HLS.

args.name: Bandwidth
args.desc: The estimated download speed; uses the run-time setting if 0.

args.name: StreamBufferingTimeout
args.desc: The maximum wait time (in seconds) before playback can begin.

args.name: DumpPath
args.desc: The directory in which the downloaded stream file is stored.

args.name: EventReportCB
args.desc: A user-defined callback function for event notifications.

args.name: AdaptiveMode
args.desc: 1 = segments are downloaded on demand (HLS); 0 = all segments are downloaded.

args.name: Duration
args.desc: The total video duration in seconds (HTTP only; improves performance).

name: web_stream_pause
signature: int web_stream_pause("ID=<n>", "PausingDuration=<secs>", LAST);
description: Pauses stream playback while keeping the current position; the stream continues to download in the background and playback resumes from the paused position. This function is not recorded automatically and must be inserted manually.

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier from web_stream_open.

args.name: PausingDuration
args.desc: The pause duration in seconds.

example:
web_stream_pause("ID=1","PausingDuration=20", LAST);
lr_vuser_status_message("Current time in movie:%lf", web_stream_get_param_double("1", CURRENT_TIME));

name: web_stream_play
signature: int web_stream_play("ID=<n>", "PlayingDuration=<seconds>", ["Speed=<n>",] LAST);
description: Plays a media stream that was opened with web_stream_open. If PlayingDuration is omitted, the entire stream is played; the step fails if the duration exceeds the step download timeout. Not recorded automatically.

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier from web_stream_open.

args.name: PlayingDuration
args.desc: The playback duration in seconds.

args.name: Speed
args.desc: The playback speed: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, or 2.0 (default 1.0).

example:
web_stream_play("ID=1", "PlayingDuration=30", "Speed=1.5", LAST);
lr_vuser_status_message("Current time:%lf", web_stream_get_param_double("1", CURRENT_TIME));

name: web_stream_seek
signature: int web_stream_seek("ID=<n>", "TimeOffset=<seconds>" | "RelativeOffset=<+/- seconds>", LAST);
description: Sets the position within a stream opened with web_stream_open, either from the start of the stream (TimeOffset) or relative to the current position (RelativeOffset). Use only one of the two; fails for live streams that do not support seeking.

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier from web_stream_open.

args.name: TimeOffset
args.desc: The position from the start of the stream (seconds).

args.name: RelativeOffset
args.desc: The offset relative to the current position (seconds, can be + or -).

name: web_stream_set_param_double
signature: int web_stream_set_param_double(const char *StreamID, const int StateType, const double StateValue);
description: Sets a new value for a double-type parameter on an open stream (for example, the SPEED). Returns LR_PASS (0) on success or LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: StreamID
args.desc: The identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: StateType
args.desc: The code of the double-type parameter, for example SPEED (13).

args.name: StateValue
args.desc: The new double value.

name: web_stream_set_param_int
signature: int web_stream_set_param_int(const char *StreamID, const int StateType, const int StateValue);
description: Sets an integer value for a parameter of an open stream, such as BANDWIDTH or BUFFERING_TIMEOUT. Not recorded automatically and does not support standard parameterization.

args.name: StreamID
args.desc: The identifier given to web_stream_open.

args.name: StateType
args.desc: The code of the integer parameter, for example BANDWIDTH (11) or BUFFERING_TIMEOUT (12).

args.name: StateValue
args.desc: The new integer value.

example:
web_stream_set_param_int("1", BANDWIDTH, 2000000);
web_stream_set_param_int("1", BUFFERING_TIMEOUT, 60);

name: web_stream_stop
signature: int web_stream_stop("ID=<n>", LAST);
description: Stops stream playback and resets the stream position to the beginning, so the next playback starts from the start. Not recorded automatically and does not support standard parameterization.

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier from web_stream_open.

example: web_stream_stop("ID=1", LAST);

name: web_stream_wait
signature: int web_stream_wait("ID=<n>", ["StreamingDuration=<seconds>"] ["Percentage=<0-100>"], LAST);
description: Holds script execution during stream playback until a specified download condition is met. Specify exactly one condition (for example, StreamingDuration or Percentage; Percentage is not supported for live streaming).

args.name: ID
args.desc: The stream identifier from web_stream_open.

args.name: StreamingDuration
args.desc: The wait duration in seconds.

args.name: Percentage
args.desc: The stream position (0-100%) to wait for.

name: web_service_call
signature: int web_service_call( const char *StepName, [URL,] ExpectedResponse, <List of specifications>, [BEGIN_ARGUMENTS, Arguments, END_ARGUMENTS,] [Send Attachments,] [BEGIN_RESULT, Results, END_RESULT,] [Receive Attachments,] LAST );
description: Calls a web service; typically generated automatically when importing a WSDL in a Web Service Vuser. Provides a high-level interface for modifying SOAP arguments. Returns LR_PASS (0) or LR_FAIL (1).

args.name: StepName
args.desc: The step name shown in the test tree.

args.name: URL
args.desc: The web service endpoint (overrides the default from the WSDL).

args.name: ExpectedResponse
args.desc: The response type: SoapResult, SoapFault, or AnySoap.

args.name: SOAPMethod
args.desc: Service|Port|Method (cannot be parameterized).

args.name: SOAPHeader
args.desc: An optional custom SOAP header in XML format.

args.name: Arguments
args.desc: Input parameters between BEGIN_ARGUMENTS and END_ARGUMENTS: ArgumentName=Value.

args.name: Results
args.desc: Output mapping between BEGIN_RESULT and END_RESULT: ResultName=ParameterName.

example:
#include "as_web.h"

web_service_call( "StepName=UkLocation",
    "ExpectedResponse=AnySoap",
    "URL=http://www.locatorx.net/uklocation.asmx",
    "SOAPMethod=TownService|TownServiceSoap|GetUKLocationByTown",
    "SOAPMethodNamespace=http://www.locatorX.NET",
    "SOAPMethodStyle=document",
    "SOAPAction=http://www.locatorX.NET/GetUKLocationByTown",
    "WSDL=http://www.locatorx.net/uklocation.asmx?WSDL",
    "SOAPHeader=<SoapHeader><e>jb14</e></SoapHeader>",
    "Snapshot=t1.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
        "Town=London",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
         "GetUKLocationByTownResult=Result",
    END_RESULT,
    LAST );

name: web_service_cancel_security
signature: int web_service_cancel_security( );
description: Cancels the security settings from a previous web_service_set_security call, so the token is no longer included in subsequent soap_request and web_service_call functions. Takes no arguments.
example:
web_service_set_security("30",
  SECURITY_TOKEN,
    "TokenName=MyUserNameToken",
    "Type=Username",
    "UserName=admin", "Password=test",
    "PasswordOptions=SendPlainText",
    "IDType=SubjectName",
  MESSAGE_SIGNATURE,
    "UseToken=MyUserNameToken",
    "TargetPath=//soap:Body/View",
    "SignatureOptions=IncludeBody|IncludeAddressing|IncludeTimestamp",
  LAST);

...

web_service_cancel_security( );

name: web_service_cancel_security_saml
signature: int web_service_cancel_security_saml();
description: A legacy function that cancels the security settings from a previous web_service_set_security_saml call, so the token is no longer included in subsequent soap_request and web_service_call functions. Takes no arguments.
example:
web_service_set_security_saml(
  "ISsuerUrl=http://myserver/SamlSecurityTokenService/SamlTokenIssuer.ashx",
  "Username=myserver\\administrator",
  "Password=abcabc",
  "PasswordOptions=SendPlainText",
  "CertStoreLocation=CurrentUser",
  "CertStoreName=AddressBook",
  "CertSubjectName=CN=WSE2QuickStartServer",
  "PolicyFile=samlPolicy.config",
  LAST );

web_service_call(
    "StepName=HelloWorld_101",
    "SOAPMethod=Service|ServiceSoap|HelloWorld",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "WSDL=http://localhost/SampleService/Service.asmx?wsdl",
    "URL=http://myserver/SampleService/Service.asmx",
    "UseWSDLCopy=1",
    "Snapshot=t1153124794.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    "HelloWorldResult=Param_HelloWorldResult",
    END_RESULT,
    LAST );

web_service_cancel_security_saml();

name: web_service_cancel_security_saml_ex
signature: int web_service_cancel_security_saml_ex( );
description: Cancels the SAML security settings from a previous web_service_set_security_saml_ex call, so the token is no longer included in subsequent soap_request and web_service_call functions. Takes no arguments.
example:
web_service_set_security_saml_ex("IssuerUrl=https://myserver/sts/STSWebHost/Saml20STSService.svc",
    "Username=test",
    "Password=test",
    "TokenType=SAML2.0",
    "KeyType=Bearer",
    "AudienceUris=https://RelyingParty/*",
    LAST);

web_service_call( "StepName=Add_101",
    "SOAPMethod=Calculator|WS2007FederationHttpBinding_ICalculator|Add",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "Service=Calculator",
    "ExpectedResponse=SoapResult",
    "Snapshot=t1568875776.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
    "n1=1",
    "n2=2",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    END_RESULT,
    LAST);

web_service_cancel_security_saml_ex();

name: web_service_set_option
signature: int web_service_set_option( const char *OptionName, const char *OptionValue );
description: Sets an option for subsequent web service calls; must be added manually before web_service_call when a particular option is needed. Returns LR_PASS (0) or LR_FAIL (1).

args.name: OptionName
args.desc: The web service option name (case-sensitive): DoNotValidateSecurity, ExcludeWseHeaders, or HandleMIMEResponse.

args.name: OptionValue
args.desc: The option value (case-insensitive), for example "true".

example:
web_service_set_option("DoNotValidateSecurity", "true");
web_service_call( "StepName=EchoBoolean_101",
    "SOAPMethod=EchoService|EchoServicePort|EchoBoolean",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "Service=EchoService",
    "ExpectedResponse=SoapResult",
    "Snapshot=t1444878757.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
    "Input=false",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    END_RESULT,
    LAST);

name: web_service_set_security
signature: int web_service_set_security ( [const char * TtlIsSeconds ,] SECURITY_TOKEN, const char * attributes, [SECURITY_TOKEN , attributes... ,] MESSAGE_SIGNATURE, const char * attributes, [MESSAGE_SIGNATURE, attributes, ...] ENCRYPTED_DATA, const char * attributes, [ENCRYPTED_DATA, attributes,...] LAST );
description: Includes a security token in all subsequent SOAP and web service requests; the token stays active until the next web_service_set_security or web_service_cancel_security call. The token is processed before attachments in each web_service_call.

args.name: TtlIsSeconds
args.desc: The message lifetime in seconds from creation.

args.name: SECURITY_TOKEN
args.desc: Defines a security token with its required attributes (Type, token name) and type-specific parameters.

args.name: MESSAGE_SIGNATURE
args.desc: Specifies token-based signing of the message or parts of the SOAP envelope.

args.name: ENCRYPTED_DATA
args.desc: Specifies token-based encryption of the message or SOAP elements.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

example:
web_service_set_security("30",
  SECURITY_TOKEN,
    "TokenName=MyUserNameToken",
    "Type=Username",
    "UserName=admin", "Password=test",
    "PasswordOptions=SendPlainText",
    "IDType=SubjectName",
  MESSAGE_SIGNATURE,
    "UseToken=MyUserNameToken",
    "TargetPath=//soap:Body/View",
    "SignatureOptions=IncludeBody|IncludeAddressing|IncludeTimestamp",
    "TransformAlgorithm=http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#",
  ENCRYPTED_DATA ,
    "EncryptionType=Content",
    "KeyAlgorithm=RSA15",
    "SessionAlgorithm=TripleDES",
  WS_ADDRESSING,
    "Version=WSA1.0",
  TIME_STAMP,
    "Exclude=True/False"
  LAST);

...

web_service_cancel_security( );

name: web_service_set_security_saml
signature: int web_service_set_security_saml([const char * IssuerURL,] [const char * Username, const char * Password,] [const char * PasswordOptions,] [const char * CertStoreLocation,] [const char * CertStoreName,] [const char * CertSubjectName,] [const char * PolicyFile,] LAST);
description: A legacy function that includes a SAML security token in subsequent SOAP/web service calls. The token is obtained from an STS endpoint and remains active until the next call or web_service_cancel_security_saml. For new scripts, use web_service_set_security_saml_ex.

args.name: IssuerURL
args.desc: The STS endpoint URL (required).

args.name: Username
args.desc: The user name for the STS.

args.name: Password
args.desc: The password for the STS.

args.name: PasswordOptions
args.desc: How the password is sent: SendPlainText, SendNone, or SendHashed.

args.name: CertStoreLocation
args.desc: The certificate store location: CurrentUser or LocalMachine.

args.name: CertStoreName
args.desc: The certificate store name.

args.name: CertSubjectName
args.desc: The certificate subject name.

args.name: PolicyFile
args.desc: The security configuration file for the RST and WebService.

example:
web_service_set_security_saml(
  "ISsuerUrl=http://myserver/SamlSecurityTokenService/SamlTokenIssuer.ashx",
  "Username=myserver\\administrator",
  "Password=abcabc",
  "PasswordOptions=SendPlainText",
  "CertStoreLocation=CurrentUser",
  "CertStoreName=AddressBook",
  "CertSubjectName=CN=WSE2QuickStartServer",
  "PolicyFile=samlPolicy.config",
  LAST );

web_service_cancel_security_saml();

name: web_service_set_security_saml_ex
signature: int web_service_set_security_saml_ex([const char * IssuerURL,] [const char * Username, const char * Password,] [const char * TokenType,] [const char * KeyType,] [const char * AudienceUris,] LAST);
description: Includes a SAML security token in subsequent SOAP/web service calls by retrieving the token from an STS endpoint. Works only with the WCF/.NET toolkit; the token remains active until the next call or web_service_cancel_security_saml_ex.

args.name: IssuerURL
args.desc: The STS endpoint URL (required).

args.name: Username
args.desc: The user name for the STS.

args.name: Password
args.desc: The password for the STS.

args.name: TokenType
args.desc: The SAML version: SAML1.1 or SAML2.0.

args.name: KeyType
args.desc: The key type: Asymmetric, Bearer, or Symmetric.

args.name: AudienceUris
args.desc: A comma-separated list of URIs agreed upon by the client and the STS.

example:
web_service_set_security_saml_ex("IssuerUrl=https://myserver/sts/STSWebHost/Saml20STSService.svc",
    "Username=test",
    "Password=test",
    "TokenType=SAML2.0",
    "KeyType=Bearer",
    "AudienceUris=https://RelyingParty/*",
    LAST);

web_service_call( "StepName=Add_101",
    "SOAPMethod=Calculator|WS2007FederationHttpBinding_ICalculator|Add",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "Service=Calculator",
    "ExpectedResponse=SoapResult",
    "Snapshot=t1568875776.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
    "n1=1",
    "n2=2",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    END_RESULT,
    LAST);

web_service_cancel_security_saml_ex();

name: web_service_wait_for_event
signature: char * web_service_wait_for_event( const char * StepName, const char * Quantifier, const char * Timeout, BEGIN_EVENTS, const char * EventName_1, [...EventName_n,] END_EVENTS, LAST );
description: Pauses script execution until a response is received from a previous asynchronous service request. Returns the name of the captured event, or null on timeout. Events are created through web_service_call (AsyncEvent=...).

args.name: StepName
args.desc: The step name in the test tree.

args.name: Quantifier
args.desc: "ALL" (wait for all events) or "ANY" (wait for the first event).

args.name: Timeout
args.desc: The maximum wait time in milliseconds.

args.name: EventName_1..n
args.desc: The list of event names, enclosed by BEGIN_EVENTS and END_EVENTS.

example:
web_service_call( "StepName=EchoString_101",
    "SOAPMethod=ExtendedECHO_rpc_encoded|ExtendedECHO_rpc_encodedSoap|EchoString",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "Service=ExtendedECHO_rpc_encoded",
    "AsyncEvent=first_event",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
    "sec=7",
    "strString=jabberwocky",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    "EchoStringResult=first_call",
    END_RESULT,
    LAST );

lr_output_message("got event %s",
    web_service_wait_for_event("StepName=WaitHere",
        "Quantifier=ALL",
        "Timeout=10000",
        BEGIN_EVENTS,
        "first_event",
        "second_event",
        END_EVENTS,
        LAST)
    );

name: ws_sign_saml_assertion
signature: int ws_sign_saml_assertion(const char *AssertionContent, const char *CertificateFile, [const char *CertificatePassword,] const char *OutParam);
description: Digitally signs a SAML assertion; it can sign an unsigned assertion or replace an existing signature. The result is saved to an output parameter.

args.name: AssertionContent
args.desc: The assertion content; if it is already signed, the old signature is replaced.

args.name: CertificateFile
args.desc: The certificate file name or full path (name only if it is in the script directory).

args.name: CertificatePassword
args.desc: The certificate file password (optional).

args.name: OutParam
args.desc: The output parameter that holds the signed SAML assertion.

name: wsdl_wsi_validation
signature: int wsdl_wsi_validation(const char *ServiceName);
description: Validates a WSDL file against the WS-I (Web Services Interoperability) standards and reports compliance. Requires the external WS-I testing tools to be installed and the service to be already imported into VuGen.

args.name: ServiceName
args.desc: The name of the imported service; the WSDL location is determined from the service import folder (supports parameterization).

example:
web_service_call( "StepName=CalcCheck",
    "SOAPMethod=Calc|CalcSoapPort|Add",
    "ResponseParam=response",
    "Service=Calc",
    "URL=http://16.59.60.46/MSSoapSamples30/Calc/Service/Rpc/IsapiCpp/Calc.WSDL",
    "ExpectedResponse=SoapResult",
    "Snapshot=t1221482536.inf",
    BEGIN_ARGUMENTS,
            "A=",
            "B=",
    END_ARGUMENTS,
    BEGIN_RESULT,
    END_RESULT,
    LAST );

wsdl_wsi_validation("ServiceName=Calc");
